`pack_padded_sequence` consumes valid prefixes: compact left-padded histories into chronological, right-padded sequences first. Supply one-dimensional CPU int64 lengths, all strictly positive; handle empty histories separately and skip packing an entirely empty batch. With `enforce_sorted=False`, PyTorch sorts internally; `pad_packed_sequence` restores the original input batch order automatically. GRU also restores returned `h_n` to that order—do not unsort again. `total_length=L` restores the requested width, but unpacked outputs remain right-padded. [Packing source](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/utils/rnn.py), [native checks](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/PackedSequence.cpp), [GRU source](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/rnn.py).

For per-position losses, map each compacted valid output back to its original left-padded position before comparing against unchanged targets. Implementation implication: use a bijective mapping over valid positions; never scatter padding entries onto valid destinations through clamped duplicate indices. Packing supports backward propagation; `scatter_` backward requires `src.shape == index.shape`, and duplicate destinations can produce incorrect gradients. After restoring left padding, read the final nonpadding position; `length-1` applies only to the compacted prefix representation. [Backward implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/PackedSequence.cpp), [scatter documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.Tensor.scatter_.html).

GRU’s built-in dropout operates between recurrent layers, excluding the last layer; it has no effect with one layer. Input/output dropout requires explicit modules. Compaction also changes recurrence compared with processing leading zero embeddings: GRU biases can update hidden state during padding. Thus packing fixes padding semantics but need not reproduce the previous training trajectory or dropout draws. [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html).
